verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses:
notes: For additional reading on these chapters, see G. B. Gray, Sacrifice in the Old Testament; A. F. Rainey, “The Order of Sacrifices in the Old Testament Ritual Texts,” Bib 51 (1970): 485-98; N. H. Snaith, The Jewish New Year Festival.

verses.zh: 「你要吩咐以色列人说：『献给我的供物，就是献给我作馨香火祭的食物，你们要按日期献给我』；
verses.en: “Command the Israelites:[NOTE:1] ‘With regard to my offering,[NOTE:2] be sure to offer[NOTE:3] my food for my offering made by fire, as a pleasing aroma to me at its appointed time.’[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and say to them.” These words have not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.

The sentence begins with the accusative “my offering.” It is suspended at the beginning as an independent accusative to itemize the subject matter. The second accusative is the formal object of the verb. It could also be taken in apposition to the first accusative.
The construction uses the imperfect tense expressing instruction, followed by the infinitive construct used to express the complement of direct object.
See L. R. Fisher, “New Ritual Calendar from Ugarit,” HTR 63 (1970): 485-501.
verses.commentary:
28:2 "You shall be careful to present My offering, My food for My offerings by fire, of a soothing aroma to Me, at their
appointed time" This chapter discusses several types of sacrifices in order, from those which occur the most often to
those which occur the least. It has been estimated that over one thousand and eighty lambs, one hundred and thirteen bulls,
thirty-two rams, thirty-two goats, one hundred and seven gallons of oil, one hundred and forty gallons of wine, and one hundred
and twelve bushels of flour are involved annually in the sacrifices of Israel. This was in addition to individual, voluntary sacrifices
(i.e., Leviticus 1-3).

- the daily morning and evening offering (i.e., "the continual"), Num. 28:2-8

- a morning offering

(1) one male lamb, one year old

(2) a tenth of an ephah of fine flour

(3) a fourth of a hin of beaten oil

(4) a fourth of a hin of strong drink

- a twilight offering of the same type as "a." above

- the Sabbath offering (mentioned only here in the Pentateuch)

- two male lambs, one year old

- two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil

- a libation

- this was in addition to #1

- the first of each month

- two bulls

- one ram

- seven male lambs, one year old

- three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull

- two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for the ram

- a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb

- a libation for each

(1) half a hin of wine for each bull

(2) a third of a hin of wine for the ram

(3) a fourth of a hin of wine for each lamb

- a male goat for a sin offering with its wine libation

- this was in addition to #1

- Passover ‒ on the 14th of the first month followed by the seven-day feast of unleavened bread, starting on the 15th

- two bulls with the accompaning offerings (see #3, d-g)

- one ram

- seven lambs

- one male goat for a sin offering

- this was in addition to #1

- these offerings were offered each day for seven days

- special holy convocation on the seventh day

- the Day of First Fruits, also known as Feast of Weeks

- a holy convocation

- two young bulls

- one ram

- seven lambs, one year old

- with their grain offerings (see #3, d-g)

- one male goat for a sin offering

- in addition to #1

See the related Special Topics.

▣ "My food" The offerings in Israel were not viewed as food for YHWH. See notes at Lev. 3:11.

▣ "at their appointed time" Each special day/offering had its appointed time (i.e., Num. 29:39). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL.

verses.zh: 又要对他们说：你们要献给耶和华的火祭，就是没有残疾、一岁的公羊羔，每日两只，作为常献的燔祭。
verses.en: You will say to them, ‘This is the offering made by fire that you must offer to the Lord: two unblemished lambs one year old each day for a continual[NOTE:1] burnt offering.
notes: The sacrifice was to be kept burning, but each morning the priests would have to clean the grill and put a new offering on the altar. So the idea of a continual burnt offering is more that of a regular offering.
verses.commentary:
28:3 "two lambs one year old without defect as a continual burnt offering every day" This is what is commonly called
"the continual" (cf. Num. 28:6). We see it first in Exod. 29:38-42. The symbol of a lamb being on the altar continually was a
symbol of God perpetually forgiving Israel's sin. Later Judaism would sacrifice a lamb at 9 AM and 3 PM.

The symbol of being "without defect" seems to mean that the lamb was innocent and it took the place of
sinful Israel. It became a type of the Messiah (cf. 2 Cor. 5:21).

verses.zh: 早晨要献一只，黄昏的时候要献一只；
verses.en: The first lamb you must offer in the morning, and the second lamb you must offer in the late afternoon,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “between the evenings” meaning between dusk and dark.
verses.commentary:
28:4 "at twilight" Literally this is "between the two evenings" (cf. Num. 28:4,8). This phrase is often used in the
discussion of the sacrificial system. It is interpreted in various ways even by the rabbis.

- Some say it is after the heat of the day.

- Some say it is between the time when the sun starts to go below the horizon and when it actually does.

- Some say it is after the sun has gone down but before the first star appears.

Option #1 seems to have been chosen by the Temple authorities because they offered a lamb at 3 PM daily.

verses.zh: 又用细面伊法十分之一，并捣成的油一欣四分之一，调和作为素祭。
verses.en: with one-tenth of an ephah[NOTE:1] of finely ground flour as a grain offering mixed with one-quarter of a hin[NOTE:2] of pressed olive oil.
notes: That is about two quarts.
That is about one quart.
verses.commentary:
28:5 "ephah. . .hin" These are two types of ancient measurements. The exact amount of each is uncertain because
the terms vary from time to time, even in the biblical material. The best source of information about measurements in Israel is
Roland deVaux's Ancient Israel Social Institutions, vol. 1. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES.

verses.zh: 这是西奈山所命定为常献的燔祭，是献给耶和华为馨香的火祭。
verses.en: It is a continual burnt offering that was instituted on Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the Lord.

verses.zh: 为这一只羊羔，要同献奠祭的酒一欣四分之一。在圣所中，你要将醇酒奉给耶和华为奠祭。
verses.en: “‘And its drink offering must be one-quarter of a hin for each lamb.[NOTE:1] You must pour out the strong drink[NOTE:2] as a drink offering to the Lord in the Holy Place.
notes: Heb “the one lamb,” but it is meant to indicate for “each lamb.”

The word שֵׁכָר (shekhar) is often translated “strong drink.” It can mean “barley beer” in the Akkadian cognate, and also in the Hebrew Bible when joined with the word for wine. English versions here read “wine” (NAB, TEV, CEV); “strong wine” (KJV); “fermented drink” (NIV, NLT); “strong drink” (ASV, NASB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
28:7 "a fourth of a hin. . .you shall pour out a libation of strong drink to the Lord" The
term "strong drink" (BDB 1016) is usually differentiated from wine. Some say that strong drink was used because wine was
not available during the wilderness wandering period.

This does refer to fermented drink (cf. Exod. 38:40). As a matter of fact, strong drink means a highly
fermented drink, which shows that fermentation itself was not evil. Here, it is used in several sacrifices. We need to rethink
our view of wine and the mind of the OT Jew (cf. Ps. 104:14-15; Pro. 31:6; Eccl. 2:3; Jdgs. 9:13; John 10:1-11; 1 Tim. 5:23).
See SPECIAL TOPIC: WINE AND STRONG DRINK.

▣ "the holy place" This refers to the outer part of the shrine tent. It held the incense altar, table of show bread,
and the lampstand. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHART OF THE TABERNACLE.

verses.zh: 晚上，你要献那一只羊羔，必照早晨的素祭和同献的奠祭献上，作为馨香的火祭，献给耶和华。」
verses.en: And the second lamb you must offer in the late afternoon; just as you offered the grain offering and drink offering in the morning,[NOTE:1] you must offer it as an offering made by fire, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
notes: Heb “as the grain offering of the morning and as its drink offering.”

verses.zh: 「当安息日，要献两只没有残疾、一岁的公羊羔，并用调油的细面伊法十分之二为素祭，又将同献的奠祭献上。
verses.en: “‘On the Sabbath day, you must offer[NOTE:1] two unblemished lambs a year old, and two-tenths of an ephah[NOTE:2] of finely ground flour as a grain offering, mixed with olive oil, along with its drink offering.
notes: The words “you must offer” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied. They have been supplied in the translation to make a complete English sentence.
That is, about 4 quarts.
verses.commentary:
28:9 "on the sabbath day" A double offering was made on the sabbath day. See Special Topics:
SABBATH (OT) and
SABBATH (NT).

verses.zh: 这是每安息日献的燔祭；那常献的燔祭和同献的奠祭在外。」
verses.en: This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath,[NOTE:1] besides the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
notes: Heb “the burnt offering of the Sabbath by its Sabbath.”

verses.zh: 「每月朔，你们要将两只公牛犊，一只公绵羊，七只没有残疾、一岁的公羊羔，献给耶和华为燔祭。
verses.en: “‘On the first day of each month[NOTE:1] you must offer as a burnt offering to the Lord two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished lambs a year old,
notes: Heb “of your months.”
verses.commentary:
28:11 "at the beginning of each of your months" This refers to the feasts known as New Moons. We can see something
of the festival in Num. 10:10.

verses.zh: 每只公牛要用调油的细面伊法十分之三作为素祭；那只公羊也用调油的细面伊法十分之二作为素祭；
verses.en: with three-tenths of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering for each bull, and two-tenths of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering for the ram,

verses.zh: 每只羊羔要用调油的细面伊法十分之一作为素祭和馨香的燔祭，是献给耶和华的火祭。
verses.en: and one-tenth of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering for each lamb, as a burnt offering for a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the Lord.

verses.zh: 一只公牛要奠酒半欣，一只公羊要奠酒一欣三分之一，一只羊羔也奠酒一欣四分之一。这是每月的燔祭，一年之中要月月如此。
verses.en: For their drink offerings, include[NOTE:1] half a hin of wine with each bull, one-third of a hin for the ram, and one-fourth of a hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month[NOTE:2] throughout the months of the year.
notes: The word “include” is not in the Hebrew text but is implied. It is supplied in the translation to make a complete English sentence.
Heb “a month in its month.”
verses.commentary:
28:14 "burnt offering. . .sin offering" We learn from Leviticus 1-5 that there are several different kinds of offerings
usually offered in sequence, each symbolizing a progress from a total consecration to forgiveness of sin and to freewill
offerings. See full notes online in Leviticus 1-5.

verses.zh: 又要将一只公山羊为赎罪祭，献给耶和华；要献在常献的燔祭和同献的奠祭以外。」
verses.en: And one male goat[NOTE:1] must be offered to the Lord as a purification offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
notes: Heb “one kid of the goats.”
verses.commentary:
28:15 "and one male goat" Literally this means "one kid of the hairy ones" (BDB 972 CONSTRUCT
BDB 777). Many translations try to make this a male but this is uncertain.

verses.zh: 「正月十四日是耶和华的逾越节。
verses.en: “‘On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Lord’s Passover.
verses.commentary:
28:16 "Passover" The Passover, recorded in Exodus 12, and further identified in Lev. 23:4-8 and Deuteronomy 16,
is combined with the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread, making it an eight-day feast. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PASSOVER.

verses.zh: 这月十五日是节期，要吃无酵饼七日。
verses.en: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the festival. For seven days bread made without yeast must be eaten.

verses.zh: 第一日当有圣会；甚么劳碌的工都不可做。
verses.en: And on the first day there is to be a holy assembly; you must do no ordinary work[NOTE:1] on it.
notes: Heb “any work [of] service”; this means any occupational work, that is, the ordinary service.

verses.zh: 当将公牛犊两只，公绵羊一只，一岁的公羊羔七只，都要没有残疾的，用火献给耶和华为燔祭。
verses.en: “‘But you must offer to the Lord an offering made by fire, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs one year old; they must all be unblemished.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “unblemished they will be to you.” So also in v. 31.

verses.zh: 同献的素祭用调油的细面；为一只公牛要献伊法十分之三；为一只公羊要献伊法十分之二；
verses.en: And their grain offering is to be of finely ground flour mixed with olive oil. For each bull you must offer three-tenths of an ephah, and two-tenths for the ram.

verses.zh: 为那七只羊羔，每只要献伊法十分之一。
verses.en: For each of the seven lambs you are to offer one-tenth of an ephah,

verses.zh: 并献一只公山羊作赎罪祭，为你们赎罪。
verses.en: as well as one goat for a purification offering, to make atonement for you.

verses.zh: 你们献这些，要在早晨常献的燔祭以外。
verses.en: You must offer these in addition to the burnt offering in the morning that is for a continual burnt offering.

verses.zh: 一连七日，每日要照这例把馨香火祭的食物献给耶和华，是在常献的燔祭和同献的奠祭以外。
verses.en: In this manner you must offer daily throughout the seven days the food of the sacrifice made by fire as a sweet aroma to the Lord. It is to be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

verses.zh: 第七日当有圣会，甚么劳碌的工都不可做。」
verses.en: On the seventh day you are to have a holy assembly, you must do no regular work.

verses.zh: 「七七节庄稼初熟，你们献新素祭给耶和华的日子，当有圣会；甚么劳碌的工都不可做。
verses.en: “‘Also, on the day of the firstfruits, when you bring a new grain offering to the Lord during your Feast of Weeks, you are to have a holy assembly. You must do no ordinary work.
verses.commentary:
28:26 "the day of the first fruits. . .Feast of Weeks" This is also discussed in Lev. 23:15-21 and is often called
Pentecost, which means "fifty," because it comes fifty days after Passover. There is some distinction between the material
in Leviticus and here in Numbers but the exact reason for the difference is uncertain. Leviticus contains the stipulations
about wave offerings, which is omitted in Numbers. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL.

verses.zh: 只要将公牛犊两只，公绵羊一只，一岁的公羊羔七只，作为馨香的燔祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: But you must offer as the burnt offering, as a sweet aroma to the Lord, two young bulls, one ram, seven lambs one year old,

verses.zh: 同献的素祭用调油的细面；为每只公牛要献伊法十分之三；为一只公羊要献伊法十分之二；
verses.en: with their grain offering of finely ground flour mixed with olive oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the one ram,

verses.zh: 为那七只羊羔，每只要献伊法十分之一。
verses.en: with one-tenth for each of the seven lambs,

verses.zh: 并献一只公山羊为你们赎罪。
verses.en: as well as one male goat to make an atonement for you.

verses.zh: 这些，你们要献在常献的燔祭和同献的素祭并同献的奠祭以外，都要没有残疾的。」
verses.en: You are to offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering—they must be unblemished.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The sacrificial system of Israel was YHWH's way to

- provide for sinful Israel to obtain forgiveness

- stay in fellowship with a holy God

- It also served as a way to remind Israel of God's presence and a way to teach their children their faith.

- These types of sacrifices showed YHWH's ownership of all things.

- time

- possessions

- crops

- land

- This is a supplement to Leviticus 23. It adds information about the daily and monthly rituals. Why it is placed here in Numbers
is uncertain.

- some suggest just before war with Midian when the Israelites would have many more animals

- just before entering Canaan where regular settled society will occur (i.e., Tabernacle or Temple worship)

- Numbers 28-29 forms a literary unit on sacrifices inserted into the historical narrative of Numbers.

- Can you imagine the smell of the sacrificial area? Can you imagine the priestly work it took to

- kill

- prepare

- offer (perform full ritual)

- clean up the ashes

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 28:1-8

1Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, 2"Command the sons of
Israel and say to them, 'You shall be careful to present My offering, My food for My offerings by fire, of a soothing aroma
to Me, at their appointed time.' 3You shall say to them, 'This is the offering by fire which you shall offer to the
Lord: two male lambs one year old without defect as a continual burnt offering every day.
4You shall offer the one lamb in the morning and the other lamb you shall offer at twilight; 5also a
tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil. 6It is a continual burnt
offering which was ordained in Mount Sinai as a soothing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord.
7Then the drink offering with it shall be a fourth of a hin for each lamb, in the holy place you shall pour out a
drink offering of strong drink to the Lord. 8The other lamb you shall offer at twilight;
as the grain offering of the morning and as its drink offering, you shall offer it, an offering by fire, a soothing aroma to the
Lord.
